9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

## Objective
- Replace the existing wasteland shooter with a complete, playable, physics-based side-scrolling off-road driving game.
- Include varied vehicles and terrain, jumps, and engine, exhaust, turbo, and NOS upgrades.

## Requirements
- Build it now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- Make the game playable and verify it with screenshots saved as small JPEGs (maximum 1280px wide); inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Replaced the shooter theme with “OVERLAND,” an endless off-road expedition with five vehicle types, procedurally varying terrain, run earnings, and a garage.
- Chose canvas-based vehicle/terrain rendering and lightweight custom driving physics; upgrade and currency persistence use `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `index.html` with the Overland game HUD, start screen, garage, crash screen, and mobile touch-control markup.
- Replaced `style.css` with responsive styling for the new game UI.
- Began replacing `game.js`: added terrain/biome generation, vehicle and upgrade data, driving physics, vehicle rendering, and other game-rendering helpers.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`: it currently ends after `draw()` and has no update/render loop, HUD updates, input/event wiring, garage actions, game start/restart flow, or persistence helpers such as `persist()` and `finishRun()` referenced by existing code.
- Run the game, fix runtime issues, and capture/inspect the requested JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- The game is not yet playable because `game.js` is incomplete and references undefined functions.

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` with input handling, the animation loop, camera, HUD/biome updates, start/crash/restart flow, and garage purchasing/equipping.
2. Implement persistence helpers and validate that all controls and gameplay systems work.
3. Launch the project, capture a small JPEG screenshot, inspect the latest image, and fix any visual or runtime defects.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Replaced game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Replaced game styling and responsive layouts.
- `game.js`: In-progress game implementation; currently incomplete.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` currently references undefined `persist()`, `finishRun()`, and `toast()`; `toast()` also needs an implementation.

## Objective
- Replace the wasteland shooter with a complete, playable, physics-based side-scrolling off-road driving game featuring varied vehicles, terrain, jumps, and upgrades.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- Verify playability and inspect only the latest screenshot, saved as a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Decisions
- The game is themed “OVERLAND,” an endless off-road expedition with five vehicle types, varied biomes, run earnings, and a garage.
- Use canvas rendering and custom driving physics; persist currency, vehicles, and upgrades with `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `index.html` with the Overland HUD, start and crash screens, garage, and touch controls.
- Replaced `style.css` with responsive styling for the new game interface.
- Added substantial terrain, biome, vehicle, rendering, and physics code to `game.js`.

### Active
- Finish `game.js`: it still lacks the main loop, input/event wiring, HUD updates, garage and run flows, and persistence functions referenced by existing code.
- Validate the game, fix runtime/visual issues, and capture and inspect the requested screenshot.

### Blocked
- The game remains unplayable until the missing JavaScript functions and event wiring are implemented.

## Next Move
1. Complete `game.js`, including `persist()`, `toast()`, `finishRun()`, HUD updates, inputs, animation loop, garage actions, and start/restart flow.
2. Run the game and fix runtime or visual defects; note `drawTerrain()` already applies `camera.y`, so the current extra `ctx.translate(0,camera.y)` in `draw()` may offset terrain incorrectly.
3. Capture a small JPEG screenshot and inspect the latest image.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Current game UI and overlay markup.
- `style.css`: Current responsive visual styling.
- `game.js`: Incomplete gameplay implementation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Two attempts to append the missing JavaScript failed because the edit tool could not match the requested text; those functions were not added.
- No game run or screenshot verification has been completed.

## Objective
- Replace the wasteland shooter with a complete, playable, physics-based side-scrolling off-road driving game featuring varied vehicles, terrain, jumps, and upgrades.
- Verify playability and inspect the latest screenshot, saved as a JPEG no wider than 1280px.

## Requirements
- Build without clarification; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.
- Capture and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- The game is themed “OVERLAND,” an endless off-road expedition with five vehicle types, varied biomes, run earnings, and a garage.
- Use canvas rendering and custom driving physics; persist currency, vehicles, and upgrades with `localStorage`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Replaced `index.html` and `style.css` with the Overland game interface, overlays, garage, HUD, and touch controls.
- Completed `game.js` with terrain, biome and vehicle rendering, driving physics, HUD, garage, input wiring, run flow, audio, and persistence.
- Fixed the extra `camera.y` translation in `draw()`.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Captured and inspected `/tmp/overland-captures/overland-latest.jpg` at 1280×800.

### Active
- Validate actual driving and confirm the latest screenshot shows the game in a representative playable state.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run the updated browser test script and confirm vehicle movement, garage interaction, and absence of runtime errors.
2. Capture and inspect a fresh JPEG at or below 1280px wide; fix any issues found.
3. Briefly summarize the result and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, physics, UI flows, persistence, and input.
- `index.html`: Game interface and overlays.
- `style.css`: Game styling and responsive layout.
- `/tmp/overland-capture.mjs`: Temporary Playwright script for gameplay/garage testing and JPEG capture.
- `/tmp/overland-captures/overland-latest.jpg`: Previously captured screenshot; should be replaced after further testing.

## Important Context
- Changes to `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` are uncommitted.
- The initial test pressing `d` for 2.5 seconds reported distance `0012` and speed `010`, so meaningful movement is not yet confirmed.
- Garage interaction was confirmed visible after pressing `g`.
- `/tmp/overland-capture.mjs` was updated to test ArrowRight for 4 seconds and check run status, but that updated script has not yet been run.
